title: Global Landscape of Registered Clinical Studies of Spatially Fractionated Radiotherapy: Evidence Gaps and Research Priorities
content: Background: Clinical investigation of spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) is expanding, but the extent to which registered interventions are defined sufficiently for replication remains unclear. We characterised the global portfolio of registered SFRT studies, assessed its evidence maturity, and identified priorities for future clinical research. Methods: We searched the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP) through 14 July 2026 as the sole global identification source. Candidate records were verified against official registry records or retained official exports, cross registry duplicates were resolved at the protocol level, and independent studies were summarised by temporal, geographic, clinical, technical, and design characteristics. Reporting completeness was assessed using a nine-domain framework and parameter-level classifications. Results: We identified 59 independent studies. Fifty (84.7%) began or were scheduled to begin in 2023–2026, with 2026 representing a partial year; 55 (93.2%) were interventional and 43 (72.9%) were non-comparative. Twenty-four studies (40.7%) evaluated SFRT alone, whereas 35 (59.3%) incorporated at least one additional protocol-defined treatment modality. Among these 35 multimodal studies, sequencing was explicitly reported in 24 (68.6%) and quantitative inter-treatment timing in 10 (28.6%). SFRT dose and fractionation were specifically or quantitatively reported in 24 studies (40.7%). All studies registered primary endpoints, but none had posted primary-registry summary results containing observed clinical endpoint values. Conclusions: The registered SFRT portfolio is expanding rapidly but remains early-stage, heterogeneous, and predominantly signal-generating. Multimodality treatment is common, whereas timing and intervention-defining technical details are incompletely reported. Future disease-specific, preferably multicentre trials should incorporate reproducible intervention definitions and transparent outcome reporting.
